newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Spain paid Bissau to take Africans - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Spain paid Bissau to take Africans - magazine.

text.p: A senior Guinea-Bissau human rights official was quoted as saying on Thursday that he had proof that Spain paid the West African state of Guinea-Bissau to receive 50 African immigrants whom it ejected in June.

"We will prove with documents that, in fact, the (Guinea-Bissau) government received money," Fernando Gomes, president of the Guinea-Bissau League for Human Rights, told the Portuguese weekly magazine Valor in an interview.
"We can prove that there were talks with the Spanish authorities," he added.
According to Gomes, the documents showed that a Spanish official delivered a sum equivalent to $165,000 to the Guinea-Bissau government.
Gomes was not immediately available to comment further as he was travelling in Brazil, an official in his office in Bissau told Reuters by telephone.
The immigrants, who say they are from six African states, are now held in cramped conditions in a jail in Bissau, capital of the former Portuguese colony, human rights officials said.
They added that the six countries rejected the efforts of the Guinea-Bissau government to repatriate the men on the grounds that they carried no identification documents.

Spain had rounded up the men at a centre for immigrants in its North African enclave of Melilla and put them on planes for Africa. After Senegal and Cameroon turned them away, they ended up in Guinea-Bissau.
Bissau rights officials have said their deportation was illegal because some had previously filled in papers in Melilla requesting travel to Spain.
The Bissau authorities had repatriated five of the original group of 50 to neighbouring Guinea, rights officials said.
The group are among hundreds of Africans who try to cross the narrow Strait of Gibraltar into Spain from North Africa every year in search of a better life in Europe.
The immigrants staged two brief hunger strikes in Bissau last month to press for their return to Spain.
